proposal.thesis: MELI is -29.4% off its 52-week high but only -5.6% off its 20-day high, sitting on its 30-week MA with volume_signal reading no_supply_pullback -- this system's own 12-year ablation found this is the one volume read with a real, repeatable edge. Two insiders (officers/directors) bought $1.19M in the open market with zero sells and zero 10b5-1 trades during the exact window the Street turned skeptical, a strong discretionary conviction signal. The Q1 margin compression (operating margin 6.91% vs 12.86% a year ago, Q ended 2026-03-31) that spooked the market is mechanically explained: roughly two-thirds is loan-loss provisioning doubling on a fast-scaling Brazil consumer credit book (an upfront GAAP reserve, not realized losses), plus deliberate logistics capex (Loggi acquisition, 14 new Brazil fulfillment centers). GMV growth is accelerating per fresh 7/22-23 coverage, FCF TTM is $11.8B (+83.1% YoY), and leverage is conservative (net_debt/EBITDA 1.67x). Citi has an active downside 30-day catalyst watch into the 8/5 print and I am trading through that print deliberately, sized small, because the print is the dated event that resolves whether this is a temporary investment cycle or a real deceleration.
catalysts: Q2 2026 earnings, 2026-08-05 -- operating margin trajectory and GMV growth confirmation/denial
Continued Brazil logistics buildout (Loggi integration, new fulfillment centers) reducing shipping cost per order over coming quarters
proposal.macro_context: SPY holds its 200-DMA (regime gate open) but sits below its 50-DMA -- a neutral, not strongly supportive tape. Momentum_health reads unwind (recent leaders being sold hard vs SPY), which is exactly why this thesis leans on an idiosyncratic, company-specific catalyst (insider buying, a name-specific earnings resolution) rather than needing the momentum factor to keep working. Falling VIX (16.6) and tightening HY spreads argue against imminent risk-off, but rising 10y/2y yields are a headwind for growth multiples generally.
proposal.risk_map: Primary risk: Citi has an active 'downside 30-day catalyst watch' into the Aug 5 print on the view that margin compression reflects rising Brazil consumer credit risk, not temporary investment -- if Q2 shows provisions still climbing as a share of the loan book alongside decelerating GMV, the bear case is confirmed and the $1,690 stop should already have fired via the structural break. Secondary risk: LatAm FX/macro (Brazil, Argentina) can move the stock independent of underlying fundamentals. Tertiary: options skew is mildly put-heavy (low confidence, free-chain data) -- a soft corroborating flag for caution, not a standalone signal.
proposal.variant_perception: CONSENSUS: Sell-side is turning cautious into the Aug 5 print -- Citi opened a 'downside 30-day catalyst watch' on 7/15 and at least one fair-value model cut its estimate from $1,827 to $1,750 citing softer revenue growth and margin assumptions, even though the 24-analyst mean target of $2,214.88 (+23.1%) has not caught up to that caution. MY VIEW: the operating-margin compression (6.91% vs 12.86% a year ago, Q ended 2026-03-31) is a deliberate investment-cycle effect, not eroding unit economics, and the stock is being penalized on the wrong metric. MECHANISM: roughly two-thirds of the margin decline is mechanical -- credit-loss provisions roughly doubled ($1,244M vs $603M) from rapidly scaling a lower-spread, longer-duration Brazil consumer loan book, which GAAP forces to reserve upfront, plus deliberate logistics capex (the Loggi acquisition, 14 new Brazil fulfillment centers, ~50% higher Brazil infra spend) that models are treating as opex bleed instead of moat-building -- the same skepticism Amazon's early fulfillment buildout drew; two insiders bought $1.19M in the open market with zero sales during this exact skepticism window, and GMV growth is accelerating per fresh 7/22-23 coverage even as headline margins compress. RESOLUTION: the Aug 5, 2026 Q2 print is the dated event -- sequential stabilization in operating margin and continued GMV acceleration confirms the temporary-investment read; continued deterioration in both, together with the live Citi catalyst window, would prove the bears right, which the stop and invalidators are built to catch early.

thesis_invalidators.invalidating_print: Q2 2026 print (due 2026-08-05) showing operating margin still below ~7% with credit-loss provisions continuing to rise as a share of the credit portfolio, or GMV growth decelerating below 35% YoY.
thesis_invalidators.invalidating_structure: A daily close below $1,690 on above-average volume, breaking the recent higher-low structure near the 200-week moving average support zone.
thesis_invalidators.time_box: If MELI has not reclaimed and held above $1,900 within 30 trading days of entry, exit and rotate the capital regardless of the earnings outcome.

proposal.thesis: Snowflake is a leading AI-data-platform name pulling back on no supply inside an intact uptrend, with fundamentals accelerating (revenue +47.6% YoY, Q ended 2026-04-30) and a 4-quarter EPS beat streak, and the sell-side visibly playing catch-up: BofA raised its target to $330 (from $300) and Jefferies to $310 (from $300), both on 2026-07-22, above both the stale bundle consensus ($298) and the current price (~$271). TTM free cash flow is positive ($1.17B) even though GAAP shows a net loss, driven by stock-based comp at 28.9% of revenue -- a real dilution cost I am weighting, not ignoring. The name sits outside today's momentum-unwind casualties (DELL/MU, hardware-side) inside the currently-accelerating software_ai sector, and options pricing shows no earnings premium built into the near-dated cycle since the next print (8/26) falls after this trade's planned exit. Institutional flow (13F + tape sponsorship) reads aligned with the rising price, and this is a pullback-continuation setup off the one volume signature my own 12-year study actually validated (no_supply_pullback).
catalysts: BofA price target raised to $330 from $300, 2026-07-22
Jefferies price target raised to $310 from $300 (Buy), 2026-07-22
Q2 FY2027 earnings 2026-08-26 (after this trade's planned exit) -- a 5th consecutive beat would confirm the acceleration thesis for the next leg
proposal.macro_context: Regime is neutral-to-supportive: SPY is above its 200-DMA (738 vs 695, +6.2%) but under its 50-DMA, 1-month flat. momentum_health flags an active factor unwind (MTUM -9.8% off its 20d high, SPMO -8.5%, vs SPY -1.8%), which the code already halves this proposal's risk budget for -- but the unwind's casualties today are DELL and MU (hardware AI suppliers hit by a negative memory-sector headline and Alphabet's capex-shock selloff), not SNOW: software_ai is instead the accelerating sector over the last few sessions (+9.6pp month-over-month). VIX is falling (-4.4% 1d) and credit spreads are tightening -- a supportive backdrop for adding measured swing risk in a name outside the specific complex under pressure.
proposal.risk_map: The central risk is that the market's 'already priced in' read on SNOW is right: it carries a rich revenue multiple and 28.9% SBC-to-revenue (Q ended 2026-04-30) with a GAAP net loss of -$295.6M, so any deceleration in consumption growth or a soft guide would compress the multiple quickly. We would know early via a break of the $253 stop on volume, a reversal in the 13F/tape sponsorship read (currently no_tracked_activity, so any shift is a real signal), or guidance commentary ahead of the 8/26 print. Director Frank Slootman's $82.3M sale this week was a cashless option exercise (dated 7/20-7/21, strike $8.88) rather than a clean discretionary sell signal, but it's a minor watch item worth tracking if it recurs.

thesis_invalidators.invalidating_structure: A daily close below the $253 stop, or a break below the rising 30-week moving average near $196, on above-average volume, invalidates the pullback-continuation setup.
thesis_invalidators.time_box: If SNOW has not reclaimed and held a daily close above $280 within 20 trading days (by 2026-08-21), exit and rotate -- the pullback-continuation thesis needs volume-confirmed follow-through, not open-ended hope.
